passages.text: So Joseph went and told Pharaoh: “My father and my brothers, with their flocks and herds and all they own, have come from the land of Canaan and are now in Goshen.”
passages.sermon:
Joseph was a son of Jacob.
Joseph served as a leader in Egypt.
Joseph went to Pharaoh.
Joseph spoke to Pharaoh.
Joseph said, "My father and my brothers have come."
They brought their flocks.
They brought their herds.
They brought everything they own.
They came from the land of Canaan.
Now they are in the land of Goshen.
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֣א יוֹסֵף֮ וַיַּגֵּ֣ד לְפַרְעֹה֒ וַיֹּ֗אמֶר אָבִ֨י וְאַחַ֜י וְצֹאנָ֤ם וּבְקָרָם֙ וְכָל־ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לָהֶ֔ם בָּ֖אוּ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ כְּנָ֑עַן וְהִנָּ֖ם בְּאֶ֥רֶץ גֹּֽשֶׁן׃

passages.text: And he chose five of his brothers and presented them before Pharaoh.
passages.sermon:
Joseph had brothers.
Joseph chose five of his brothers.
Joseph took these five brothers.
Joseph brought them to Pharaoh.
Joseph presented these five brothers before Pharaoh.
passages.original: וּמִקְצֵ֣ה אֶחָ֔יו לָקַ֖ח חֲמִשָּׁ֣ה אֲנָשִׁ֑ים וַיַּצִּגֵ֖ם לִפְנֵ֥י פַרְעֹֽה׃

passages.text: “What is your occupation?” Pharaoh asked Joseph’s brothers. “Your servants are shepherds,” they replied, “both we and our fathers.”
passages.sermon:
Pharaoh spoke to Joseph’s brothers.
Pharaoh asked them a question.
Pharaoh said, “What is your occupation?”
Joseph’s brothers answered Pharaoh.
They said, “We are your servants.”
They said, “We are shepherds.”
They said, “Our fathers were shepherds too.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֧אמֶר פַּרְעֹ֛ה אֶל־ אֶחָ֖יו מַה־ מַּעֲשֵׂיכֶ֑ם וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ אֶל־ פַּרְעֹ֗ה רֹעֵ֥ה צֹאן֙ עֲבָדֶ֔יךָ גַּם־ אֲנַ֖חְנוּ גַּם־ אֲבוֹתֵֽינוּ׃

passages.text: Then they said to Pharaoh, “We have come to live in the land for a time, because there is no pasture for the flocks of your servants, since the famine in the land of Canaan has been severe. So now, please allow your servants to settle in the land of Goshen.”
passages.sermon:
Joseph’s brothers spoke to Pharaoh.
They said, “We have come to live in this land for a time.
There is no pasture for the flocks of your servants.
The famine in the land of Canaan is very severe.
Please let your servants settle in the land of Goshen.”
passages.original: וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ אֶל־ פַּרְעֹ֗ה לָג֣וּר בָּאָרֶץ֮ בָּאנוּ֒ כִּי־ אֵ֣ין מִרְעֶ֗ה לַצֹּאן֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לַעֲבָדֶ֔יךָ כִּֽי־ כָבֵ֥ד הָרָעָ֖ב בְּאֶ֣רֶץ כְּנָ֑עַן וְעַתָּ֛ה יֵֽשְׁבוּ־ נָ֥א עֲבָדֶ֖יךָ בְּאֶ֥רֶץ גֹּֽשֶׁן׃

passages.text: Pharaoh said to Joseph, “Now that your father and brothers have come to you, the land of Egypt is before you; settle your father and brothers in the best part of the land. They may dwell in the land of Goshen. And if you know of any talented men among them, put them in charge of my own livestock.”
passages.sermon:
Pharaoh spoke to Joseph.
Pharaoh said, “Your father and your brothers have come to you.”
Pharaoh ruled Egypt.
Pharaoh had authority over the land.
Pharaoh said, “The land of Egypt is open before you.”
Pharaoh said, “Settle your father and your brothers in the best part of the land.”
Pharaoh said, “Let them live in the land of Goshen.”
Pharaoh said, “If you know any capable men among them, appoint them as overseers of my livestock.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר פַּרְעֹ֔ה אֶל־ יוֹסֵ֖ף לֵאמֹ֑ר אָבִ֥יךָ וְאַחֶ֖יךָ בָּ֥אוּ אֵלֶֽיךָ׃ אֶ֤רֶץ מִצְרַ֙יִם֙ לְפָנֶ֣יךָ הִ֔וא בְּמֵיטַ֣ב הָאָ֔רֶץ הוֹשֵׁ֥ב אֶת־ אָבִ֖יךָ וְאֶת־ אַחֶ֑יךָ יֵשְׁבוּ֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ גֹּ֔שֶׁן וְאִם־ יָדַ֗עְתָּ וְיֶשׁ־ בָּם֙ אַנְשֵׁי־ חַ֔יִל וְשַׂמְתָּ֛ם שָׂרֵ֥י מִקְנֶ֖ה עַל־ אֲשֶׁר־ לִֽי׃

passages.text: Then Joseph brought in his father Jacob and presented him before Pharaoh, and Jacob blessed Pharaoh.
passages.sermon:
Joseph was the son of Jacob.
Joseph brought his father Jacob to Pharaoh.
Joseph presented Jacob before Pharaoh.
Jacob blessed Pharaoh.
passages.original: וַיָּבֵ֤א יוֹסֵף֙ אֶת־ יַֽעֲקֹ֣ב אָבִ֔יו וַיַּֽעֲמִדֵ֖הוּ לִפְנֵ֣י פַרְעֹ֑ה וַיְבָ֥רֶךְ יַעֲקֹ֖ב אֶת־ פַּרְעֹֽה׃

passages.text: “How many years have you lived?” Pharaoh asked.
passages.sermon:
Pharaoh was the king of Egypt.
Pharaoh spoke to Jacob.
Pharaoh asked Jacob a question.
Pharaoh said, “How many years have you lived?”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר פַּרְעֹ֖ה אֶֽל־ יַעֲקֹ֑ב כַּמָּ֕ה יְמֵ֖י שְׁנֵ֥י חַיֶּֽיךָ׃

passages.text: “My travels have lasted 130 years,” Jacob replied. “My years have been few and hard, and they have not matched the years of the travels of my fathers.”
passages.sermon:
Jacob spoke to Pharaoh.
Jacob was the father of Joseph.
Jacob was an old man.
Jacob said, “I have lived as a traveler for 130 years.”
“My years have been few.”
“My years have been hard.”
“My life has not been as long as the lives of my fathers.”
“My fathers lived as travelers longer than I have.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יַעֲקֹב֙ אֶל־ פַּרְעֹ֔ה יְמֵי֙ שְׁנֵ֣י מְגוּרַ֔י שְׁלֹשִׁ֥ים וּמְאַ֖ת שָׁנָ֑ה מְעַ֣ט וְרָעִ֗ים הָיוּ֙ יְמֵי֙ שְׁנֵ֣י חַיַּ֔י וְלֹ֣א הִשִּׂ֗יגוּ אֶת־ יְמֵי֙ שְׁנֵי֙ חַיֵּ֣י אֲבֹתַ֔י בִּימֵ֖י מְגוּרֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: Then Jacob blessed Pharaoh and departed from his presence.
passages.sermon: Jacob stood before Pharaoh.\r\nJacob blessed Pharaoh.\r\nJacob left Pharaoh’s presence.
passages.original: וַיְבָ֥רֶךְ יַעֲקֹ֖ב אֶת־ פַּרְעֹ֑ה וַיֵּצֵ֖א מִלִּפְנֵ֥י פַרְעֹֽה׃

passages.text: So Joseph settled his father and brothers in the land of Egypt and gave them property in the best part of the land, the district of Rameses, as Pharaoh had commanded.
passages.sermon:
Joseph was the son of Jacob.
Joseph had brothers.
Pharaoh was the ruler of Egypt.
Pharaoh gave a command.
Joseph obeyed Pharaoh’s command.
Joseph settled his father and his brothers in Egypt.
Joseph gave his father and brothers property in Egypt.
Joseph gave them property in the best part of the land.
This best part was the district of Rameses.
passages.original: וַיּוֹשֵׁ֣ב יוֹסֵף֮ אֶת־ אָבִ֣יו וְאֶת־ אֶחָיו֒ וַיִּתֵּ֨ן לָהֶ֤ם אֲחֻזָּה֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם בְּמֵיטַ֥ב הָאָ֖רֶץ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ רַעְמְסֵ֑ס כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר צִוָּ֥ה פַרְעֹֽה׃

passages.text: Joseph also provided his father and brothers and all his father’s household with food for their families.
passages.sermon:
Joseph was the son of Jacob.
Joseph lived in Egypt.
Joseph gave food to his father.
Joseph gave food to his brothers.
Joseph gave food to all his father’s household.
Joseph gave each family the amount of food they needed.
passages.original: וַיְכַלְכֵּ֤ל יוֹסֵף֙ אֶת־ אָבִ֣יו וְאֶת־ אֶחָ֔יו וְאֵ֖ת כָּל־ בֵּ֣ית אָבִ֑יו לֶ֖חֶם לְפִ֥י הַטָּֽף׃

passages.text: There was no food, however, in all that region, because the famine was so severe; the lands of Egypt and Canaan had been exhausted by the famine.
passages.sermon:
There was no food in the land.
A very severe famine struck the region.
The land of Egypt suffered because of the famine.
The land of Canaan also suffered because of the famine.
The famine exhausted both Egypt and Canaan.
passages.original: וְלֶ֤חֶם אֵין֙ בְּכָל־ הָאָ֔רֶץ כִּֽי־ כָבֵ֥ד הָרָעָ֖ב מְאֹ֑ד וַתֵּ֜לַהּ אֶ֤רֶץ מִצְרַ֙יִם֙ וְאֶ֣רֶץ כְּנַ֔עַן מִפְּנֵ֖י הָרָעָֽב׃

passages.text: Joseph collected all the money to be found in the land of Egypt and the land of Canaan in exchange for the grain they were buying, and he brought it into Pharaoh’s palace.
passages.sermon:
Joseph was in charge in Egypt.
Joseph also had authority in Canaan.
Joseph collected all the money in Egypt.
Joseph collected all the money in Canaan.
People gave money to buy grain.
Joseph took the money they paid for grain.
Joseph brought all the money to Pharaoh’s palace.
passages.original: וַיְלַקֵּ֣ט יוֹסֵ֗ף אֶת־ כָּל־ הַכֶּ֙סֶף֙ הַנִּמְצָ֤א בְאֶֽרֶץ־ מִצְרַ֙יִם֙ וּבְאֶ֣רֶץ כְּנַ֔עַן בַּשֶּׁ֖בֶר אֲשֶׁר־ הֵ֣ם שֹׁבְרִ֑ים וַיָּבֵ֥א יוֹסֵ֛ף אֶת־ הַכֶּ֖סֶף בֵּ֥יתָה פַרְעֹֽה׃

passages.text: When the money from the lands of Egypt and Canaan was gone, all the Egyptians came to Joseph and said, “Give us food. Why should we die before your eyes? For our funds have run out!”
passages.sermon:
A severe famine struck Egypt and Canaan.
There was no food in either land.
People in both lands spent all their money to buy grain.
The money in Egypt and Canaan ran out.
All the Egyptians went to Joseph.
Joseph was the governor of Egypt.
The Egyptians spoke to Joseph.
They said, “Give us food.”
They said, “Why should we die in front of you?”
They said, “We have no money left.”
passages.original: וַיִּתֹּ֣ם הַכֶּ֗סֶף מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַיִם֮ וּמֵאֶ֣רֶץ כְּנַעַן֒ וַיָּבֹאוּ֩ כָל־ מִצְרַ֨יִם אֶל־ יוֹסֵ֤ף לֵאמֹר֙ הָֽבָה־ לָּ֣נוּ לֶ֔חֶם וְלָ֥מָּה נָמ֖וּת נֶגְדֶּ֑ךָ כִּ֥י אָפֵ֖ס כָּֽסֶף׃

passages.text: “Then bring me your livestock,” said Joseph. “Since the money is gone, I will sell you food in exchange for your livestock.”
passages.sermon:
Joseph was the ruler in Egypt under Pharaoh.
Joseph spoke to the people of Egypt.
He said, “Bring me your livestock.
I will give you food in exchange for your livestock.
You have no money left.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יוֹסֵף֙ הָב֣וּ מִקְנֵיכֶ֔ם וְאֶתְּנָ֥ה לָכֶ֖ם בְּמִקְנֵיכֶ֑ם אִם־ אָפֵ֖ס כָּֽסֶף׃

passages.text: So they brought their livestock to Joseph, and he gave them food in exchange for their horses, their flocks and herds, and their donkeys. Throughout that year he provided them with food in exchange for all their livestock.
passages.sermon:
Joseph was the governor of Egypt during a severe famine.
The Egyptians had no money left to buy food.
They brought their livestock to Joseph.
They gave Joseph their horses.
They gave Joseph their flocks of sheep and goats.
They gave Joseph their herds of cattle.
They gave Joseph their donkeys.
Joseph gave them food in exchange for their animals.
Joseph provided them with food for the entire year.
He did this in return for all their livestock.
passages.original: וַיָּבִ֣יאוּ אֶת־ מִקְנֵיהֶם֮ אֶל־ יוֹסֵף֒ וַיִּתֵּ֣ן לָהֶם֩ יוֹסֵ֨ף לֶ֜חֶם בַּסּוּסִ֗ים וּבְמִקְנֵ֥ה הַצֹּ֛אן וּבְמִקְנֵ֥ה הַבָּקָ֖ר וּבַחֲמֹרִ֑ים וַיְנַהֲלֵ֤ם בַּלֶּ֙חֶם֙ בְּכָל־ מִקְנֵהֶ֔ם בַּשָּׁנָ֖ה הַהִֽוא׃

passages.text: When that year was over, they came to him the second year and said, “We cannot hide from our lord that our money is gone and all our livestock belongs to you. There is nothing left for our lord except our bodies and our land.
passages.sermon:
The Egyptians suffered a severe famine.
Joseph was the governor of Egypt.
The people came to Joseph after one year ended.
They came to him in the second year of famine.
They spoke to Joseph.
They said, “We cannot hide the truth from you, our lord.
Our money is gone.
All our livestock now belongs to you, our lord.
We have nothing left for you, our lord.
Only our bodies and our land remain.”
passages.original: וַתִּתֹּם֮ הַשָּׁנָ֣ה הַהִוא֒ וַיָּבֹ֨אוּ אֵלָ֜יו בַּשָּׁנָ֣ה הַשֵּׁנִ֗ית וַיֹּ֤אמְרוּ לוֹ֙ לֹֽא־ נְכַחֵ֣ד מֵֽאֲדֹנִ֔י כִּ֚י אִם־ תַּ֣ם הַכֶּ֔סֶף וּמִקְנֵ֥ה הַבְּהֵמָ֖ה אֶל־ אֲדֹנִ֑י לֹ֤א נִשְׁאַר֙ לִפְנֵ֣י אֲדֹנִ֔י בִּלְתִּ֥י אִם־ גְּוִיָּתֵ֖נוּ וְאַדְמָתֵֽנוּ׃

passages.text: Why should we perish before your eyes—we and our land as well? Purchase us and our land in exchange for food. Then we, along with our land, will be slaves to Pharaoh. Give us seed that we may live and not die, and that the land may not become desolate.”
passages.sermon:
The Egyptians spoke to Joseph.
They were suffering from a severe famine.
They said, “Why should we die before your eyes?
We do not want ourselves and our land to perish.
Buy us and our land in exchange for food.
If you do this, we and our land will become slaves to Pharaoh.
Give us seed so we can plant crops.
Then we will live and not die.
The land will not become empty and desolate.”
passages.original: לָ֧מָּה נָמ֣וּת לְעֵינֶ֗יךָ גַּם־ אֲנַ֙חְנוּ֙ גַּ֣ם אַדְמָתֵ֔נוּ קְנֵֽה־ אֹתָ֥נוּ וְאֶת־ אַדְמָתֵ֖נוּ בַּלָּ֑חֶם וְנִֽהְיֶ֞ה אֲנַ֤חְנוּ וְאַדְמָתֵ֙נוּ֙ עֲבָדִ֣ים לְפַרְעֹ֔ה וְתֶן־ זֶ֗רַע וְנִֽחְיֶה֙ וְלֹ֣א נָמ֔וּת וְהָאֲדָמָ֖ה לֹ֥א תֵשָֽׁם׃

passages.text: So Joseph acquired for Pharaoh all the land in Egypt; the Egyptians, one and all, sold their fields because the famine was so severe upon them. The land became Pharaoh’s, and Joseph reduced the people to servitude from one end of Egypt to the other.
passages.sermon:
Joseph served as a ruler in Egypt under Pharaoh.
A severe famine struck Egypt.
The famine was very strong.
The Egyptians could not survive without help.
Each Egyptian sold his field to Joseph.
Joseph bought all the land in Egypt for Pharaoh.
The land now belonged to Pharaoh.
Joseph moved the people into cities.
He moved them from one end of Egypt to the other.
passages.original: וַיִּ֨קֶן יוֹסֵ֜ף אֶת־ כָּל־ אַדְמַ֤ת מִצְרַ֙יִם֙ לְפַרְעֹ֔ה כִּֽי־ מָכְר֤וּ מִצְרַ֙יִם֙ אִ֣ישׁ שָׂדֵ֔הוּ כִּֽי־ חָזַ֥ק עֲלֵהֶ֖ם הָרָעָ֑ב וַתְּהִ֥י הָאָ֖רֶץ לְפַרְעֹֽה׃ וְאֶ֨ת־ הָעָ֔ם הֶעֱבִ֥יר אֹת֖וֹ לֶעָרִ֑ים מִקְצֵ֥ה גְבוּל־ מִצְרַ֖יִם וְעַד־ קָצֵֽהוּ׃

passages.text: However, he did not acquire the priests’ portion of the land, for it had been given to them by Pharaoh. They ate the rations that Pharaoh supplied; so they did not sell their land.
passages.sermon:
Joseph did not buy the land of the priests.
Pharaoh gave the priests a portion of land.
Pharaoh provided food for the priests.
The priests ate the food Pharaoh gave them.
The priests did not sell their land.
passages.original: רַ֛ק אַדְמַ֥ת הַכֹּהֲנִ֖ים לֹ֣א קָנָ֑ה כִּי֩ חֹ֨ק לַכֹּהֲנִ֜ים מֵאֵ֣ת פַּרְעֹ֗ה וְאָֽכְל֤וּ אֶת־ חֻקָּם֙ אֲשֶׁ֨ר נָתַ֤ן לָהֶם֙ פַּרְעֹ֔ה עַל־ כֵּ֕ן לֹ֥א מָכְר֖וּ אֶת־ אַדְמָתָֽם׃

passages.text: Then Joseph said to the people, “Now that I have acquired you and your land for Pharaoh this day, here is seed for you to sow in the land.
passages.sermon:
Joseph was the governor of Egypt.
\r\nJoseph spoke to the people of Egypt.
\r\nJoseph said, "Today I have bought you for Pharaoh."
\r\nJoseph said, "I have also bought your land for Pharaoh."
\r\nJoseph said, "I give you seed."
\r\nJoseph said, "You will plant this seed in the land."
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יוֹסֵף֙ אֶל־ הָעָ֔ם הֵן֩ קָנִ֨יתִי אֶתְכֶ֥ם הַיּ֛וֹם וְאֶת־ אַדְמַתְכֶ֖ם לְפַרְעֹ֑ה הֵֽא־ לָכֶ֣ם זֶ֔רַע וּזְרַעְתֶּ֖ם אֶת־ הָאֲדָמָֽה׃

passages.text: At harvest time, you are to give a fifth of it to Pharaoh, and four-fifths will be yours as seed for the field and food for yourselves and your households and children.”
passages.sermon:
Joseph spoke to the people of Egypt.
Joseph had acquired their land for Pharaoh.
Joseph gave the people seed to plant in the land.
Joseph set a rule for the harvest.
At harvest time, the people must give one-fifth of the crops to Pharaoh.
The people may keep four-fifths of the crops.
The people will use this portion as seed for the fields.
The people will also use this portion for food.
The people will feed themselves with it.
The people will feed everyone in their households with it.
The people will feed their children with it.
passages.original: וְהָיָה֙ בַּתְּבוּאֹ֔ת וּנְתַתֶּ֥ם חֲמִישִׁ֖ית לְפַרְעֹ֑ה וְאַרְבַּ֣ע הַיָּדֹ֡ת יִהְיֶ֣ה לָכֶם֩ לְזֶ֨רַע הַשָּׂדֶ֧ה וּֽלְאָכְלְכֶ֛ם וְלַאֲשֶׁ֥ר בְּבָתֵּיכֶ֖ם וְלֶאֱכֹ֥ל לְטַפְּכֶֽם׃

passages.text: “You have saved our lives,” they said. “We have found favor in our lord’s eyes, and we will be Pharaoh’s servants.”
passages.sermon:
The people of Egypt spoke to Joseph.
Joseph had saved their lives during a time of famine.
The people said, "You have saved our lives."
They said, "We have found favor in your eyes, our lord."
They said, "We will be servants to Pharaoh."
passages.original: וַיֹּאמְר֖וּ הֶחֱיִתָ֑נוּ נִמְצָא־ חֵן֙ בְּעֵינֵ֣י אֲדֹנִ֔י וְהָיִ֥ינוּ עֲבָדִ֖ים לְפַרְעֹֽה׃

passages.text: So Joseph established a law that a fifth of the produce belongs to Pharaoh, and it is in effect in the land of Egypt to this day. Only the priests’ land does not belong to Pharaoh.
passages.sermon:
Joseph was a ruler in Egypt.
Joseph made a law in Egypt.
This law says that one fifth of the produce belongs to Pharaoh.
This law still exists in Egypt today.
Pharaoh owns the land and receives a fifth of its produce.
The priests have their own land.
Pharaoh does not own the priests’ land.
passages.original: וַיָּ֣שֶׂם אֹתָ֣הּ יוֹסֵ֡ף לְחֹק֩ עַד־ הַיּ֨וֹם הַזֶּ֜ה עַל־ אַדְמַ֥ת מִצְרַ֛יִם לְפַרְעֹ֖ה לַחֹ֑מֶשׁ רַ֞ק אַדְמַ֤ת הַכֹּֽהֲנִים֙ לְבַדָּ֔ם לֹ֥א הָיְתָ֖ה לְפַרְעֹֽה׃

passages.text: Now the Israelites settled in the land of Egypt, in the region of Goshen. They acquired property there and became fruitful and increased greatly in number.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites were God's chosen people.
They settled in the land of Egypt.
They lived in the region called Goshen.
They acquired property in Goshen.
They became fruitful in the land.
They increased greatly in number.
passages.original: וַיֵּ֧שֶׁב יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל בְּאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרַ֖יִם בְּאֶ֣רֶץ גֹּ֑שֶׁן וַיֵּאָחֲז֣וּ בָ֔הּ וַיִּפְר֥וּ וַיִּרְבּ֖וּ מְאֹֽד׃

passages.text: And Jacob lived in the land of Egypt seventeen years, and the length of his life was 147 years.
passages.sermon:
Jacob was the father of Joseph.
Jacob lived in the land of Egypt.
He lived there for seventeen years.
Jacob’s total lifespan was one hundred forty-seven years.
passages.original: וַיְחִ֤י יַעֲקֹב֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם שְׁבַ֥ע עֶשְׂרֵ֖ה שָׁנָ֑ה וַיְהִ֤י יְמֵֽי־ יַעֲקֹב֙ שְׁנֵ֣י חַיָּ֔יו שֶׁ֣בַע שָׁנִ֔ים וְאַרְבָּעִ֥ים וּמְאַ֖ת שָׁנָֽה׃

passages.text: When the time drew near for Israel to die, he called his son Joseph and said to him, “If I have found favor in your eyes, put your hand under my thigh and promise to show me kindness and faithfulness. Do not bury me in Egypt, but when I lie down with my fathers, carry me out of Egypt and bury me with them.” Joseph answered, “I will do as you have requested.”
passages.sermon:
Israel was also called Jacob.
Israel was the father of Joseph.
The time came near for Israel to die.
Israel called his son Joseph to him.
Israel spoke to Joseph.
Israel said, “If I have found favor in your eyes, do something for me.
Put your hand under my thigh.
Promise to show me kindness and faithfulness.
Do not bury me in Egypt.
When I die, I will be with my fathers.
Carry me out of Egypt.
Bury me with my fathers.”
Joseph answered Israel.
Joseph said, “I will do as you have requested.”
passages.original: וַיִּקְרְב֣וּ יְמֵֽי־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֘ל לָמוּת֒ וַיִּקְרָ֣א׀ לִבְנ֣וֹ לְיוֹסֵ֗ף וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לוֹ֙ אִם־ נָ֨א מָצָ֤אתִי חֵן֙ בְּעֵינֶ֔יךָ שִֽׂים־ נָ֥א יָדְךָ֖ תַּ֣חַת יְרֵכִ֑י וְעָשִׂ֤יתָ עִמָּדִי֙ חֶ֣סֶד וֶאֱמֶ֔ת אַל־ נָ֥א תִקְבְּרֵ֖נִי בְּמִצְרָֽיִם׃ וְשָֽׁכַבְתִּי֙ עִם־ אֲבֹתַ֔י וּנְשָׂאתַ֙נִי֙ מִמִּצְרַ֔יִם וּקְבַרְתַּ֖נִי בִּקְבֻרָתָ֑ם וַיֹּאמַ֕ר אָנֹכִ֖י אֶֽעֱשֶׂ֥ה כִדְבָרֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: “Swear to me,” Jacob said. So Joseph swore to him, and Israel bowed in worship at the head of his bed.
passages.sermon:
Jacob was also called Israel.
Jacob spoke to Joseph.
Jacob said, “Swear to me.”
Joseph made an oath to Jacob.
Israel bowed in worship.
Israel bowed at the head of his bed.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר הִשָּֽׁבְעָה֙ לִ֔י וַיִּשָּׁבַ֖ע ל֑וֹ וַיִּשְׁתַּ֥חוּ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל עַל־ רֹ֥אשׁ הַמִּטָּֽה׃פ
